title: How it works
text:
Each neighborhood (Census block group) is colored by the fastest scheduled trip to Binghamton University’s main campus: walking to a nearby BC Transit stop, plus the bus ride.
The four views:

Groceries (Saturday): the faster of walking straight to a supermarket (up to 800 m) or taking the bus to one, arriving by noon.
To campus, weekday: arriving on campus by 8am on a Tuesday.
To campus, Saturday: arriving by noon.
Leaving campus, weeknight: leaving between 10 and 11pm. BC Transit’s last bus off campus leaves at 8:31pm, so almost every neighborhood shows no access.

title: How it works
text:
Data

Bus schedules: BC Transit’s public GTFS feed (Broome County).
Neighborhoods: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates (2020–2024).
Supermarkets: OpenStreetMap (shop=supermarket), spot-checked against store directories.
OCCT schedules (night headline only): OCCT Fall 2026 schedule, checked October 2026. Not part of the map.

title: How it works
text:
Assumptions and limits

Riders walk up to 800 m (about 11 minutes) to a stop, at 1.2 m/s.
Each neighborhood is measured from one point inside it, so large rural areas are approximate.
Times are based on schedules, not real-time bus locations.
Some stop times are estimated between scheduled timepoints.
OCCT (the student bus system) is not included, because its schedules aren’t in BC Transit’s data. Student neighborhoods are better connected than this map shows, especially late at night.
Census numbers are survey estimates with margins of error.

title: Getting Around Binghamton Without a Car
Getting Around Binghamton Without a Car
text:
At night
BC Transit’s last bus out of campus on weekdays leaves at 8:31 pm. After that, only OCCT runs: to the West Side and Downtown until 11:45 pm, but to the Southside and Johnson City’s Main Street only until 9:35 pm. Sunday through Thursday, nothing runs after midnight (OCCT Fall 2026 schedule).

title: Getting Around Binghamton Without a Car
text:
The map
Based on BC Transit’s schedule for Tuesday, October 20, 2026 and Saturday, October 24, 2026.
Pick a view in the box on the map. Each neighborhood is colored by the fastest trip by bus, including the walk to the stop. On Saturdays, about 82% of Broome County’s car-free households can reach a supermarket within 30 minutes, by bus or on foot.






Warning



OCCT isn’t on this map. It shows BC Transit only, since OCCT’s schedules aren’t in BC Transit’s data. Students living near OCCT routes have more options than shown, especially on the West Side.
